newsitem.title: UK: Lazard Freres could sell Pearson stake - FT.
newsitem.headline: Lazard Freres could sell Pearson stake - FT.

text.p: LONDON, Jan 11 (Reuter ) - French investment bank Lazard Freres may sell its stake in Pearson Plc if the British conglomerate decides to give up its investment banking interests, Michel David-Weill, the senior partner of Lazard Freres, said on Saturday.
He made the comment in an interview published in the Financial Times. Pearson, which owns the Financial Times, has nine percent of Lazard Freres.

Marjorie Scardino took over as chief executive of Pearson on January 8 and analysts have speculated that she could move to sell off its banking interests, which also include a 50 percent stake in London's Lazard Brothers.
David-Weill said he would prefer Pearson to hold on to its stake in Lazard Freres, but if it chose to sell the bank would want to buy the stock itself and would need to finance the purchase.
"Logically", Lazard might sell its Pearson stake to find the necessary funds, he said, but it would not sell "to a party which could be hostile".

The newspaper put the value of Lazard Freres' stake in Pearson at 360 million pounds ($605 million). In all, the linked Lazard investment banks in Paris, London and New York owned 48 million Pearson shares, it said.
David-Weill said the value of these was equivalent to the value of Pearson's Lazard stake. -- London Newsroom +44 171 542 7717 ($1=.5950 Pound)
